title: Help Paying for Heat
intro: Heating costs a lot in Maine winters. Help comes from a few places. Check your income, then follow the steps in order.

emergency.lowFuelText: Call the local agency now to book an appointment:
emergency.dangerText: Call 911. For help finding fuel funds any time, dial 211.

income.title: Check your income first
income.text: Heating, repair and sealing programs use the same limit. Add up everyone's income before taxes.
income.fine: Over the limit? You may be able to subtract some medical costs. More than 6 people? See the official chart.

checklist.title: Get these ready
items: Proof of income for everyone in your home, and your other money records
Your fuel type and your fuel dealer's name
Names and birth dates for everyone in your home
checklist.note: Bring all of your financial records to your appointment. Each program may ask for more, so check its official page.

steps.title: Last stop
steps.sub: Only when other programs are not enough

programs.name: The Opportunity Alliance
programs.summary: Takes heating applications for Cumberland County, which includes Westbrook. Call first to make an appointment. Please do not walk in.

programs.name: Home Energy Assistance Program (HEAP)
programs.summary: Help paying part of your heating bill. The money goes to your fuel dealer. It does not cover the whole winter.
programs.know: Homeowners and renters under the income limit. Apply from August through May.

programs.name: Energy Crisis Intervention Program (ECIP)
programs.chip: Waiting on funding, expected in November
programs.summary: Emergency fuel when you are almost out. You need an approved HEAP application first. It usually opens November 1.
programs.know: This year the agency is waiting to hear about funding, which it expects sometime in November 2026. The start date and amount will be shared when they are announced. Until then, call to ask.

programs.name: Central Heating Improvement Program (CHIP)
programs.summary: Money to repair or replace a heating system. Homes with no heat come first.
programs.know: Some households pay part of the cost.

programs.name: Weatherization Assistance
programs.summary: A free home energy check, then work like sealing air leaks and adding insulation.
programs.know: Renters need the landlord to agree to the work.

programs.name: Efficiency Maine insulation rebates
programs.chip: No income limit for basic rebates
programs.summary: Rebates for insulation and air sealing. Lower income households get bigger rebates.
programs.know: A registered Efficiency Maine vendor must do the work.

programs.name: Veterans’ Emergency Financial Assistance
programs.chip: Based on need, not a set income limit
programs.summary: One-time emergency money for Maine veterans with no savings or other help.
programs.know: Ask if heating costs count. Contact Easterseals Maine.

programs.name: 211 Maine
programs.summary: A free help line that can point you to local fuel funds and help set up a fuel delivery.
programs.know: You can also text your ZIP code to 898-211.

programs.name: Westbrook General Assistance
programs.summary: City help for basic needs like heat when other programs are not enough. Appointment only, no walk-ins.
programs.know: Based on income for 30 days at a time. You must apply to other programs first.
